components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and language, as in 说, 语, 请; 访 is to visit and ask.
方 (fāng) hints at the sound: 访 fǎng is close, as in 仿 fǎng and 纺 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 记者今天采访了他。
example.pinyin: Jìzhě jīntiān cǎifǎng le tā.
example.english: The reporter interviewed him today.
example.fact: 访 is bound: 访问 (visit), 采访 (interview), 拜访 (call on), 访客 (visitor). 拜访 is respectful, used when visiting someone of higher status.

examples.hanzi: 下周我要去上海访问客户。
examples.pinyin: Xiàzhōu wǒ yào qù Shànghǎi fǎngwèn kèhù.
examples.english: Next week I am going to Shanghai to visit clients.

examples.hanzi: 他去乡下采访了一位老人。
examples.pinyin: Tā qù xiāngxia cǎifǎng le yí wèi lǎorén.
examples.english: He went to the countryside to interview an old man.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 召 itself sounds out 招 zhāo, 照 zhào and 超 chāo.
刀 (dāo) is only a loose sound clue for zhào.

example.hanzi: 老师召集大家开会。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zhàojí dàjiā kāihuì.
example.english: The teacher called everyone together for a meeting.
example.fact: 召 is formal and appears in 召开 (to convene), 召唤 (summon), 号召 (call upon) and 召回 (recall a product).

examples.hanzi: 公司明天召开全体大会。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī míngtiān zhàokāi quántǐ dàhuì.
examples.english: The company will hold an all-staff meeting tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 他的话召唤了很多年轻人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà zhàohuàn le hěn duō niánqīng rén.
examples.english: His words called out to many young people.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 渴 is thirst, a need for water.
曷 (hé) — near sound — 渴 is kě; 曷 also sounds out 喝 hē.

example.hanzi: 我又渴又饿。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yòu kě yòu è.
example.english: I'm both thirsty and hungry.
example.fact: 渴 also means longing, in 渴望 (to long for) and 渴求. 口渴 is 'thirsty', and the idiom 临渴掘井 means 'dig a well only when thirsty'.

examples.hanzi: 跑了一个小时，我渴死了。
examples.pinyin: Pǎo le yí ge xiǎoshí, wǒ kě sǐ le.
examples.english: After running for an hour, I am dying of thirst.

examples.hanzi: 天气太热了，我特别渴，想喝冰水。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì tài rè le, wǒ tèbié kě, xiǎng hē bīngshuǐ.
examples.english: Are you thirsty? Do you want some water?

components.note: 重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).
见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.

example.hanzi: 这家公司非常重视员工的健康。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī fēicháng zhòngshì yuángōng de jiànkāng.
example.english: This company places great importance on employees' health.
example.fact: Finland has consistently ranked among the top countries in international workplace well-being surveys, partly because Finnish labor law guarantees generous parental leave and mandates regular rest breaks, reflecting a national culture that places heavy institutional value on worker health. Comparative OECD studies often cite Finland alongside other Nordic countries as a benchmark for balancing productivity with well-being.

examples.hanzi: 老师很重视学生的意见。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī hěn zhòngshì xuésheng de yìjiàn.
examples.english: The teacher values students' opinions.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该重视环境保护问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi zhòngshì huánjìng bǎohù wèntí.
examples.english: We should take environmental protection seriously.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 流 is flowing water.
㐬 (liú) — same sound — 流 is liú; 㐬 also sounds out 琉 liú and 硫 liú.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and waves: 河, 海, 汤; 浪 is a wave.
良 (liáng) is a loose clue; also in 狼 láng, 朗 lǎng and 娘 niáng.

example.hanzi: 这只流浪狗被好心人收养了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī liúlàng gǒu bèi hǎoxīnrén shōuyǎngle.
example.english: This stray dog was adopted by a kind-hearted person.
example.fact: Moscow's stray dog population became famous for a small number of individuals that learned to ride the city's subway system, boarding trains at one stop and exiting closer to reliable food sources. Researchers who studied the behavior in the 2000s found the dogs used sound and scheduling cues, adapting an entirely human transit system to their own survival needs.

examples.hanzi: 他一个人流浪了很多年。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī gè rén liúlàng le hěn duō nián.
examples.english: He wandered alone for many years.

examples.hanzi: 街上流浪的小猫需要有人照顾。
examples.pinyin: Jiē shàng liúlàng de xiǎomāo xūyào yǒurén zhàogù.
examples.english: The stray kittens on the street need someone to take care of them.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室; 完 first meant complete, whole.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; 元 also sounds out 玩 wán, 院 yuàn and 远 yuǎn.
子 (child) — 了 is usually read as a swaddled baby, like 子 without the arms. Its meanings 'finish' (了解 liǎo) and the particle le were borrowed later.

example.hanzi: 手机掉进水里,完了。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī diàojìn shuǐ lǐ, wánle.
example.english: The phone fell into the water — it's done for.
example.fact: Most modern smartphones are not actually destroyed by water immersion itself but by the short circuits that occur afterward when the device is powered on while still wet, which is why manufacturers and repair technicians almost universally recommend leaving a soaked phone off and drying out for at least 24 hours before attempting to turn it on again.

examples.hanzi: 完了，我忘记带钥匙了！
examples.pinyin: Wánle, wǒ wàngjì dài yàoshi le!
examples.english: Oh no, I forgot my keys!

examples.hanzi: 这次考试要是不及格就完了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì yàoshi bù jígé jiù wánle.
examples.english: If I fail this exam, I'm done for.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
令 (order) — a person kneeling under a command from above. Its sound spreads to 冷 lěng, 零 líng, 铃 líng, 领 lǐng and 怜 lián.

example.hanzi: 将军下令全军立刻撤退。
example.pinyin: Jiāngjūn xiàlìng quánjūn lìkè chètuì.
example.english: The general ordered the entire army to retreat immediately.
example.fact: In 1940, facing near-certain defeat at Dunkirk, the German high command controversially halted its advancing panzer divisions for several days, an order historians still debate the reasoning behind, which gave British and French forces time to organize the evacuation of over 330,000 troops across the English Channel.

examples.hanzi: 市长下令关闭所有的学校。
examples.pinyin: Shìzhǎng xiàlìng guānbì suǒyǒu de xuéxiào.
examples.english: The mayor ordered all the schools closed.

examples.hanzi: 老板下令今天必须完成这个项目。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn xiàlìng jīntiān bìxū wánchéng zhège xiàngmù.
examples.english: The boss ordered that this project be finished today.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
水 (water) — a picture of flowing water; as a radical it appears as 氵 on the left (海, 河) or 水 at the bottom (泉, 冰).
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 城市的下水道系统需要定期维护。
example.pinyin: Chéngshì de xiàshuǐdào xìtǒng xūyào dìngqī wéihù.
example.english: The city's sewer system needs regular maintenance.
example.fact: Ancient Rome's Cloaca Maxima, built around the 6th century BC to drain marshes and carry away waste, is considered one of the world's earliest large-scale sewer systems, and parts of its stone channels still exist and function beneath modern Rome today. Its construction was a major reason the city could grow as densely as it did in antiquity.

examples.hanzi: 暴雨让下水道堵住了，街上积了水。
examples.pinyin: Bàoyǔ ràng xiàshuǐdào dǔ zhù le, jiē shàng jī le shuǐ.
examples.english: The heavy rain blocked the sewer and water gathered in the street.

examples.hanzi: 他的戒指不小心掉进了下水道。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jièzhi bù xiǎoxīn diào jìn le xiàshuǐdào.
examples.english: His ring accidentally fell into the drain.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants, the deep green of grass; also in 草 grass, 花 flower.
仓 (cāng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 沧 cāng and 舱 cāng.
虫 (insect) — creatures, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake.
黾 (mǐn, toad) is only a loose sound clue for yíng.

example.hanzi: 厨房里飞进来一只苍蝇。
example.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ fēijìnlái yì zhī cāngying.
example.english: A housefly flew into the kitchen.
example.fact: Houseflies can taste with receptors located on their feet, meaning they effectively sample a surface's chemistry the instant they land on it, which is part of why they seem to check out food so quickly before deciding whether to eat. Their compound eyes also process motion far faster than human eyes, letting them dodge swats that would easily catch a slower-reacting insect.

examples.hanzi: 别让苍蝇落在食物上。
examples.pinyin: Bié ràng cāngying luò zài shíwù shàng.
examples.english: Don't let flies land on the food.

examples.hanzi: 夏天房间里总有很多苍蝇。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān fángjiān lǐ zǒng yǒu hěn duō cāngying.
examples.english: There are always lots of flies in the room in summer.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 脚 foot, 脸 face.
退 (tuì) gives the same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他跑步时大腿肌肉拉伤了。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎobù shí dàtuǐ jīròu lāshāngle.
example.english: He strained his thigh muscle while running.
example.fact: The femur, the bone running through the thigh, is the longest and strongest bone in the human body, able to withstand roughly 1,800 kilograms (about 4,000 pounds) of compressive force before fracturing under laboratory testing — several times the average adult's body weight.

examples.hanzi: 她摔倒时大腿受了伤。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuāidǎo shí dàtuǐ shòu le shāng.
examples.english: She injured her thigh when she fell.

examples.hanzi: 这条裤子的大腿部分太紧了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi de dàtuǐ bùfen tài jǐn le.
examples.english: The thigh part of these trousers is too tight.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees; 杜 first named a pear tree, as in 树 tree, 林 forest.
土 (tǔ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 肚 dù.
女 (woman) — traditional reading shows an axe-like weapon 戌 over a woman 女, hence power and authority; compare 姑 and 妈.

example.hanzi: 图书馆采用杜威十进分类法整理图书。
example.pinyin: Túshūguǎn cǎiyòng Dùwēi shíjìn fēnlèifǎ zhěnglǐ túshū.
example.english: The library organizes its books using the Dewey Decimal Classification.
example.fact: The Dewey Decimal System, created by American librarian Melvil Dewey in 1876, organizes library books into ten broad numbered categories that can be subdivided endlessly with decimal points, and it remains in active use in tens of thousands of libraries worldwide despite being nearly 150 years old.

examples.hanzi: 杜威是美国著名的教育家和哲学家。
examples.pinyin: Dùwēi shì Měiguó zhùmíng de jiàoyùjiā hé zhéxuéjiā.
examples.english: Dewey was a famous American educator and philosopher.

examples.hanzi: 你认识那位叫杜威的足球运动员吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi nà wèi jiào Dùwēi de zúqiú yùndòngyuán ma?
examples.english: Do you know the football player named Du Wei?

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
⺮ (bamboo) — 竹 (bamboo) as in 笔, 筷, 篮; boxes and baskets were woven from bamboo, so 箱 is a box or chest.
相 (xiāng) — same sound — 箱 is xiāng, just like 相.

example.hanzi: 请把包裹放进信箱里。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ bāoguǒ fàngjìn xìnxiāng lǐ.
example.english: Please put the package in the mailbox.
example.fact: The color of mailboxes varies widely by country and carries historical meaning: red boxes in the United Kingdom trace back to Victorian-era standardization in the 1870s so they could be spotted easily against most backgrounds, while the blue mailboxes of the United States were adopted more recently, in 1955, replacing an older olive-green design.

examples.hanzi: 我每天下班都会检查一下信箱。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān xiàbān dōu huì jiǎnchá yīxià xìnxiāng.
examples.english: I check my mailbox every day after work.

examples.hanzi: 你的电子信箱满了，收不到新邮件。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de diànzǐ xìnxiāng mǎn le, shōu bù dào xīn yóujiàn.
examples.english: Your email inbox is full and can't receive new mail.

components.note: 米 (rice) — refined grain gives the idea of essence and the best part, hence 精 fine, spirit (精神).
青 (qīng) is a near sound match (-ing); the series 青 清 请 情 晴 静 helps recall jīng.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 显微镜下可以看到精子的活动。
example.pinyin: Xiǎnwēijìng xià kěyǐ kàndào jīngzǐ de huódòng.
example.english: Sperm cell movement can be observed under a microscope.
example.fact: Human sperm cells are among the smallest cells in the body, yet they must travel a relatively enormous distance — roughly 15 to 18 centimeters through the female reproductive tract — a journey proportionally comparable to a human swimming several kilometers, which is one reason only a tiny fraction ever reach an egg.

examples.hanzi: 医生用显微镜检查了精子的数量。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng yòng xiǎnwēijìng jiǎnchá le jīngzǐ de shùliàng.
examples.english: The doctor used a microscope to check the sperm count.

examples.hanzi: 生物课上，老师讲了精子和卵子的结合。
examples.pinyin: Shēngwù kè shàng, lǎoshī jiǎng le jīngzǐ hé luǎnzǐ de jiéhé.
examples.english: In biology class, the teacher explained how sperm and egg combine.

components.note: 火 (fire) — what is left after a fire dies down: ash; 灰 also sounds out 恢 huī.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 天空变成了灰色,好像要下雨了。
example.pinyin: Tiānkōng biànchéngle huīsè, hǎoxiàng yào xiàyǔ le.
example.english: The sky turned gray, as if it were about to rain.
example.fact: African elephants owe part of their gray color to a thick layer of skin up to 2.5 centimeters deep that they regularly coat in dust and mud, which both protects against sunburn and helps regulate body temperature, giving their already gray hide an even duller, matted appearance in the wild.

examples.hanzi: 他穿了一件灰色的毛衣。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān le yī jiàn huīsè de máoyī.
examples.english: He wore a gray sweater.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题有很多灰色地带。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí yǒu hěn duō huīsè dìdài.
examples.english: This issue has many gray areas.

components.note: 巴 (bā) — 巴 gives the sound bā in 爸 bà, 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 疤 bā, so it is a useful sound clue.
土 (earth) — earth radical — a base is something solid on the ground, as in 地, 城, 块.
其 (qí) — loose hint — 基 is jī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth and ground, as in 地, 城, 块; 坦 is level ground, then open and frank.
旦 (dàn) — near sound — 坦 is tǎn; 旦 also sounds out 但 dàn and 担 dān.

example.hanzi: 巴基斯坦位于南亚地区。
example.pinyin: Bājīsītǎn wèiyú Nányà dìqū.
example.english: Pakistan is located in South Asia.
example.fact: K2, the world's second-highest mountain at 8,611 meters, sits on the border between Pakistan and China and is considered far more dangerous to climb than Everest, with a historical fatality rate among summiteers of roughly one in four, earning it the nickname "Savage Mountain."

examples.hanzi: 巴基斯坦和中国是友好的邻国。
examples.pinyin: Bājīsītǎn hé Zhōngguó shì yǒuhǎo de línguó.
examples.english: Pakistan and China are friendly neighbors.

examples.hanzi: 他去巴基斯坦参观过很多古迹。
examples.pinyin: Tā qù Bājīsītǎn cānguān guo hěn duō gǔjì.
examples.english: He visited many historic sites in Pakistan.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 我们终于可以面对面交谈了。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngyú kěyǐ miànduìmiàn jiāotán le.
example.english: We can finally talk face to face.
example.fact: Psychologists studying communication have found that face-to-face conversation conveys emotional tone through combined channels — facial expression, tone of voice, and body posture — that phone calls and text messages strip away one by one, which is part of why misunderstandings are statistically more common in text-based exchanges than in in-person conversation.

examples.hanzi: 我更喜欢面对面地跟朋友聊天。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gèng xǐhuan miàn duì miàn de gēn péngyou liáotiān.
examples.english: I prefer chatting with friends face to face.

examples.hanzi: 两个对手面对面地坐在了谈判桌前。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng gè duìshǒu miànduìmiàn de zuò zài le tánpànzhuō qián.
examples.english: The two opponents sat face to face at the negotiating table.

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.

example.hanzi: 修理电线时要小心电击。
example.pinyin: Xiūlǐ diànxiàn shí yào xiǎoxīn diànjī.
example.english: Be careful of electric shock when repairing wires.
example.fact: The electric eel, despite its name actually a type of knifefish, can generate discharges of up to 860 volts, among the strongest bioelectric shocks of any animal, using thousands of specialized cells called electrocytes stacked like tiny batteries along its body to stun prey and deter predators.

examples.hanzi: 被电击了一下，我的手麻了。
examples.pinyin: Bèi diànjī le yīxià, wǒ de shǒu má le.
examples.english: I got an electric shock and my hand went numb.

examples.hanzi: 医生用电击帮助他恢复了心跳。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng yòng diànjī bāngzhù tā huīfù le xīntiào.
examples.english: The doctor used electric shock to restore his heartbeat.

meanings: to be born in the year of

components.note: 尸 (body, building) — dwelling and body words: 居, 屋, 层; 属 is to belong to a family or group.
Traditional 屬 had 蜀 (shǔ) as sound part, also in 独 dú, 烛 zhú, 触 chù; simplified 属 keeps the reading shǔ.

example.hanzi: 我属龙，你属什么？
example.pinyin: Wǒ shǔ lóng, nǐ shǔ shénme?
example.english: I'm a dragon; what are you?
example.fact: 你属什么? is how Chinese people ask someone's zodiac sign. 属于 means 'to belong to', 金属 is 'metal'. It can also be read zhǔ, in literary words.

examples.hanzi: 你属什么？我属马。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shǔ shénme? Wǒ shǔ mǎ.
examples.english: What is your zodiac sign? I am a Horse.

examples.hanzi: 这些书都属于图书馆。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shū dōu shǔyú túshūguǎn.
examples.english: These books all belong to the library.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.

example.hanzi: 达尔文提出了生物进化的理论。
example.pinyin: Dá'ěrwén tíchūle shēngwù jìnhuà de lǐlùn.
example.english: Darwin proposed the theory of biological evolution.
example.fact: Charles Darwin published "On the Origin of Species" in 1859, but he had actually developed the core idea of natural selection two decades earlier, delaying publication partly out of caution over its controversial implications until a letter from fellow naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace, independently arriving at a similar theory, prompted him to finally go public.

examples.hanzi: 科学家研究了鸟类的进化过程。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā yánjiū le niǎolèi de jìnhuà guòchéng.
examples.english: Scientists studied the evolution of birds.

examples.hanzi: 手机在十年里进化得非常快。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī zài shí nián lǐ jìnhuà de fēicháng kuài.
examples.english: Phones have evolved very fast in ten years.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is the base; the loose sound clue also appears in 趣 qù and 娶 qǔ. The top 日 here is an old cap shape, not the sun.
亻 (person) — a person bowing low; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
氐 (dī) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 底 dǐ and 抵 dǐ.

example.hanzi: 今天的最低气温是零下五度。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de zuìdī qìwēn shì língxià wǔ dù.
example.english: Today's lowest temperature is minus five degrees.
example.fact: The lowest natural air temperature ever recorded on Earth's surface was -89.2°C (-128.6°F), measured at the Soviet Vostok Station in Antarctica in 1983, a spot so cold and dry that exposed skin can suffer frostbite within minutes and diesel fuel would freeze solid without special additives.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的最低消费是五十块。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de zuìdī xiāofèi shì wǔshí kuài.
examples.english: This shop's minimum spend is fifty yuan.

examples.hanzi: 这个月他的成绩降到了最低。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè tā de chéngjì jiàng dào le zuìdī.
examples.english: This month his grades dropped to the lowest.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 这本小说将于下个月正式发行。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn xiǎoshuō jiāngyú xià ge yuè zhèngshì fāxíng.
example.english: This novel will be officially published next month.
example.fact: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press, developed around 1440 in Mainz, Germany, made it possible to issue multiple identical copies of a text far faster than hand-copying, and historians estimate that within 50 years of its invention, tens of millions of books had been printed across Europe — a scale of publishing unimaginable before.

examples.hanzi: 这家银行下个月发行新的信用卡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā yínháng xià gè yuè fāxíng xīn de xìnyòngkǎ.
examples.english: This bank will issue a new credit card next month.

examples.hanzi: 这张专辑在全国同时发行。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuānjí zài quánguó tóngshí fāxíng.
examples.english: This album is being released nationwide at the same time.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — twisting by hand; also in 拧 wring, 拉 pull.
丑 (chǒu) is a loose clue; 纽 niǔ and 钮 niǔ share it and sound exactly like 扭.
曲 (bent) — the shape pictures something bent; qū means crooked and qǔ means a song, as in 歌曲.

example.hanzi: 强烈的磁场会扭曲指南针的方向。
example.pinyin: Qiángliè de cíchǎng huì niǔqū zhǐnánzhēn de fāngxiàng.
example.english: A strong magnetic field will distort the compass's direction.
example.fact: According to Einstein's general theory of relativity, massive objects like stars and planets actually distort the fabric of spacetime itself, bending the paths of light and nearby objects — an effect confirmed in 1919 when astronomers observed starlight curving as it passed near the sun during a solar eclipse.

examples.hanzi: 他把事实扭曲了，让大家误会了我。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ shìshí niǔqū le, ràng dàjiā wùhuì le wǒ.
examples.english: He distorted the facts and made everyone misunderstand me.

examples.hanzi: 疼痛让他的脸扭曲了。
examples.pinyin: Téngtòng ràng tā de liǎn niǔqū le.
examples.english: The pain twisted his face.

components.note: 十 (ten) — complete and wide: 博 is broad, abundant.
尃 (fū) is a loose sound clue for bó; 尃 also in 搏 bó, 薄 báo and 缚 fù.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; a guest is a person under your roof.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 路 lù, 洛 luò, 落 luò.

example.hanzi: 她开了一个关于旅行的博客。
example.pinyin: Tā kāile yí ge guānyú lǜxíng de bókè.
example.english: She started a blog about traveling.
example.fact: The word "weblog" was coined in 1997 by programmer Jorn Barger, and it was later shortened to "blog" in 1999 by Peter Merholz, who split the word playfully as "we blog" in a post on his own site — a casual joke that ended up naming an entire medium.

examples.hanzi: 他每天都在博客上写一篇日记。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān dōu zài bókè shàng xiě yī piān rìjì.
examples.english: He writes a diary entry on his blog every day.

examples.hanzi: 这个美食博客有很多读者。
examples.pinyin: Zhège měishí bókè yǒu hěn duō dúzhě.
examples.english: This food blog has many readers.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.

example.hanzi: 他是我最好的好友。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de hǎoyǒu.
example.english: He is my very best friend.
example.fact: A famous long-running Harvard study that has tracked hundreds of men since 1938 found that the strength of close personal relationships, more than wealth or fame, was the single strongest predictor of health and happiness in later life, a conclusion the study's directors have highlighted repeatedly across more than 80 years of data.

examples.hanzi: 你可以把她加为好友。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ bǎ tā jiā wéi hǎoyǒu.
examples.english: You can add her as a friend.

examples.hanzi: 我和好友约好周末去看电影。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé hǎoyǒu yuē hǎo zhōumò qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: I made plans with a close friend to see a movie on the weekend.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 肝 liver, 脸, 腿; 脾 is the spleen, and by extension temper.
卑 (bēi) hints at the sound: 脾 pí is close to 牌 pái and 啤 pí.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.hanzi: 他因为一点小事就对同事发脾气。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi yìdiǎn xiǎoshì jiù duì tóngshì fāpíqi.
example.english: He lost his temper at a colleague over a trivial matter.
example.fact: Neuroscientists have found that during an angry outburst, activity in the brain's prefrontal cortex — the region responsible for impulse control and rational judgment — tends to drop while the amygdala, tied to fear and aggression, becomes more active, which helps explain why people often say things in anger they later regret.

examples.hanzi: 你别对孩子发脾气，他还小。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié duì háizi fā píqi, tā hái xiǎo.
examples.english: Don't lose your temper with the child, he's still small.

examples.hanzi: 她今天心情不好，动不动就发脾气。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān xīnqíng bù hǎo, dòngbudòng jiù fā píqi.
examples.english: She's in a bad mood today and flares up at the slightest thing.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 住; 偷 is a person stealing.
俞 (yú) is a loose hint for tōu; 愉 yú and 输 shū share it.
穴 (cave, hole) — creeping in through a hole; also in 空 empty, 窗 window.
切 (qiè) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 商店安装了摄像头以防止偷窃。
example.pinyin: Shāngdiàn ānzhuāngle shèxiàngtóu yǐ fángzhǐ tōuqiè.
example.english: The store installed cameras to prevent theft.
example.fact: The Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum theft of 1990, in which thieves disguised as police officers stole 13 artworks worth an estimated $500 million, remains the largest unsolved art theft in history, and the museum still displays the empty frames on its walls as a standing invitation for the missing pieces' return.

examples.hanzi: 他因为偷窃被商店的保安抓住了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi tōuqiè bèi shāngdiàn de bǎo'ān zhuā zhù le.
examples.english: He was caught by the shop's security for theft.

examples.hanzi: 偷窃是违法的行为。
examples.pinyin: Tōuqiè shì wéifǎ de xíngwéi.
examples.english: Stealing is illegal.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
子 (child) — on the left. 孔 means a hole or opening; 孔子 is Confucius, whose surname is 孔.
乚 (a hook) — the dictionary story is a baby's mouth, unproven. Memory aid: a child with a hook-shaped opening, a small hole.

example.hanzi: 多年不见,他的面孔已经变了很多。
example.pinyin: Duōnián bújiàn, tā de miànkǒng yǐjīng biànle hěn duō.
example.english: After years apart, his face had changed a lot.
example.fact: Humans are remarkably specialized at recognizing faces, relying on a dedicated brain region called the fusiform face area that activates far more strongly for faces than for almost any other visual category, which is also why humans are prone to "face pareidolia" — seeing faces in clouds, rock formations, or everyday objects.

examples.hanzi: 他的面孔看起来有点熟悉。
examples.pinyin: Tā de miànkǒng kàn qǐlái yǒudiǎn shúxī.
examples.english: His face looks a bit familiar.

examples.hanzi: 教室里出现了几张新面孔。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoshì lǐ chūxiàn le jǐ zhāng xīn miànkǒng.
examples.english: A few new faces appeared in the classroom.

meanings: Columbia (name of various entities, mostly in the USA)

components.note: 可 (kě) doubled — a loose sound hint for gē. The same 哥 sounds out 歌 gē (song).
亻 (person) — person radical — 伦 is about human relations and order, 伦理 ethics.
仑 (lún) — same sound — 仑 also sounds out 轮 lún and 论 lùn.
比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.
亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.

example.hanzi: 哥伦比亚是世界上咖啡产量最高的国家之一。
example.pinyin: Gēlúnbǐyà shì shìjiè shàng kāfēi chǎnliàng zuì gāo de guójiā zhīyī.
example.english: Colombia is one of the countries with the highest coffee production in the world.
example.fact: Colombia's mountainous terrain and equatorial climate give it two coffee harvests a year in many regions, unlike most coffee-growing countries that harvest only once, which is a major reason the country has remained among the world's top coffee exporters for over a century.

examples.hanzi: 哥伦比亚的咖啡味道很香。
examples.pinyin: Gēlúnbǐyà de kāfēi wèidao hěn xiāng.
examples.english: Colombian coffee has a rich aroma.

examples.hanzi: 他在哥伦比亚大学读研究生。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài Gēlúnbǐyà Dàxué dú yánjiūshēng.
examples.english: He is doing a master's degree at Columbia University.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — 羊 is a symbol of good fortune, as in 美 and 祥; 善 is goodness and kindness, together with 口 (words).
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 她善于处理复杂的人际关系。
example.pinyin: Tā shànyú chǔlǐ fùzá de rénjì guānxi.
example.english: She is good at handling complex interpersonal relationships.
example.fact: Octopuses are famously skilled problem-solvers despite having no centralized brain structure comparable to vertebrates; roughly two-thirds of their neurons are distributed throughout their arms, letting each arm process sensory information and make some decisions independently while still coordinating with the rest of the body.

examples.hanzi: 他善于跟不同的人沟通。
examples.pinyin: Tā shànyú gēn bùtóng de rén gōutōng.
examples.english: He is good at communicating with different people.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子善于观察，总能发现新东西。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi shànyú guānchá, zǒng néng fāxiàn xīn dōngxi.
examples.english: This child is good at observing and always discovers new things.

components.note: 黄 (huáng) — yellow; as a part it sounds out 簧 huáng and 磺 huáng.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — marks liquids and things that flow, as in 河 river, 汤 soup, 酒 liquor; here an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) sounds exactly like 油 — the same sound clue appears in 邮 yóu and 柚 yòu.

example.hanzi: 妈妈在面包上涂了一层黄油。
example.pinyin: Māma zài miànbāo shàng túle yì céng huángyóu.
example.english: Mom spread a layer of butter on the bread.
example.fact: Making one pound of butter requires roughly 21 pints of milk, since butter is essentially the concentrated fat skimmed and churned out of cream, and archaeological evidence suggests humans have been churning butter for at least 4,000 years, with ancient butter remains even found preserved in Irish peat bogs.

examples.hanzi: 做蛋糕需要先把黄油放软。
examples.pinyin: Zuò dàngāo xūyào xiān bǎ huángyóu fàng ruǎn.
examples.english: To make a cake, you first need to soften the butter.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢在烤面包上抹黄油和果酱。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài kǎo miànbāo shàng mǒ huángyóu hé guǒjiàng.
examples.english: He likes spreading butter and jam on toast.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 推 is to push.
隹 (zhuī) is a loose hint for tuī; 堆 duī and 谁 shéi share it.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 迟 is slow going, late.
尺 (chǐ) is a close sound match, tone differs.

example.hanzi: 由于天气原因,航班被推迟了。
example.pinyin: Yóuyú tiānqì yuányīn, hángbān bèi tuīchíle.
example.english: The flight was postponed due to weather conditions.
example.fact: The 2020 Tokyo Olympics were postponed by a full year, to 2021, marking the first time in the modern Games' history that an Olympics was delayed rather than outright cancelled, a decision driven by the global COVID-19 pandemic and made only about four months before the original opening ceremony.

examples.hanzi: 他们把婚礼推迟到了明年春天。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen bǎ hūnlǐ tuīchí dào le míngnián chūntiān.
examples.english: They postponed the wedding until next spring.

examples.hanzi: 请不要把今天的工作推迟到明天。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bù yào bǎ jīntiān de gōngzuò tuīchí dào míngtiān.
examples.english: Please don't put off today's work until tomorrow.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 车 is a cart or vehicle, as in 轮, 输, 车; 转 is turning of wheels.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 转 is zhuǎn; 专 also sounds out 传 chuán and 砖 zhuān.
车 (cart) — 车 is a cart or vehicle, as in 轮, 输, 车; 转 is turning of wheels.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 转 is zhuǎn; 专 also sounds out 传 chuán and 砖 zhuān.

example.hanzi: 吃完饭我们出去转转吧。
example.pinyin: Chī wán fàn wǒmen chūqù zhuànzhuan ba.
example.english: Let's go out for a stroll after we finish eating.
example.fact: A short walk after a meal has a measurable physiological benefit: several clinical studies have found that walking for just 10 to 15 minutes after eating can meaningfully lower the resulting spike in blood sugar compared with remaining seated, an effect linked to muscles absorbing glucose from the bloodstream during light activity.

examples.hanzi: 周末我想在老城区转转。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xiǎng zài lǎo chéngqū zhuànzhuan.
examples.english: On the weekend I'd like to stroll around the old town.

examples.hanzi: 你先到处转转，我去停车。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān dàochù zhuànzhuan, wǒ qù tíngchē.
examples.english: You look around first while I go park.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 进入这个区域需要特别通行证。
example.pinyin: Jìnrù zhège qūyù xūyào tèbié tōngxíngzhèng.
example.english: Entering this area requires a special pass.
example.fact: During the Cold War, East German citizens needed rarely granted passes to cross into West Berlin, and when travel restrictions were unexpectedly announced as lifted on November 9, 1989, tens of thousands of people rushed the checkpoints that same night without waiting for passes at all, effectively ending the wall's control almost overnight.

examples.hanzi: 没有通行证，保安不让我们进去。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu tōngxíngzhèng, bǎo'ān bù ràng wǒmen jìnqù.
examples.english: Without a pass, the guard won't let us in.

examples.hanzi: 他申请到了一张入境通行证。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēnqǐng dào le yī zhāng rùjìng tōngxíngzhèng.
examples.english: He got an entry permit.

components.note: 火 (fire) — roasting over flames; also in 烧 burn, 煮 cook.
考 (kǎo) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 拷 kǎo and 铐 kào.
肉 — a picture of a slab of meat with its grain lines; as a left-hand radical it shrinks to ⺼ in 脸, 腿, 肌.

example.hanzi: 周末我们打算在院子里烤肉。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen dǎsuàn zài yuànzi lǐ kǎoròu.
example.english: This weekend we plan to barbecue in the yard.
example.fact: Archaeological evidence suggests early humans were cooking meat over fire at least 780,000 years ago at a site in modern-day Israel, and some researchers argue that the ability to cook food fundamentally changed human evolution by making calories easier to digest, possibly enabling the brain growth seen in later hominins.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的烤肉特别香。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de kǎoròu tèbié xiāng.
examples.english: The barbecued meat at this place smells especially good.

examples.hanzi: 我们晚上去吃韩国烤肉怎么样？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshang qù chī Hánguó kǎoròu zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: How about Korean barbecue tonight?

components.note: 母 (mǔ) is a close sound clue for měi; the same part also in 海 hǎi, 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 每人都能领到一份礼物。
example.pinyin: Měi rén dōu néng lǐng dào yī fèn lǐwù.
example.english: Everyone can receive a gift.
example.fact: The human body sheds roughly 30,000 to 40,000 skin cells every minute. Over the course of a decade, a person effectively replaces their entire outer layer of skin many times over, and household dust is partly made up of these shed cells.

examples.hanzi: 这些苹果每人只能拿两个。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē píngguǒ měi rén zhǐ néng ná liǎng gè.
examples.english: Everyone can only take two of these apples.

examples.hanzi: 每人五十块，一共两百块。
examples.pinyin: Měi rén wǔshí kuài, yīgòng liǎng bǎi kuài.
examples.english: Fifty yuan per person, two hundred in total.

components.note: 缶 (clay jar) — marks pots and jars, as in 罐 jar, 缸 vat; a chipped jar is 缺, lacking.
夬 (guài/jué) is a loose hint for quē; 决 jué and 快 kuài share it.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 每个人都有自己的缺点。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de quēdiǎn.
example.english: Everyone has their own shortcomings.
example.fact: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington collapsed in 1940 just months after opening, brought down by a design flaw that let wind trigger violent aerodynamic oscillations — a shortcoming that reshaped how engineers test bridges in wind tunnels ever since.

examples.hanzi: 这款手机最大的缺点是电池不耐用。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī zuì dà de quēdiǎn shì diànchí bù nàiyòng.
examples.english: This phone's biggest drawback is its short battery life.

examples.hanzi: 你要学会接受自己的缺点。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào xuéhuì jiēshòu zìjǐ de quēdiǎn.
examples.english: You need to learn to accept your own flaws.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talking: 说, 计, 谈; 设 is to set up or plan by instruction.
殳 (shū, hand holding a tool) is only a loose sound clue; also in 投 tóu and 股 gǔ.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 你可以在手机里设定闹钟。
example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài shǒujī lǐ shèdìng nàozhōng.
example.english: You can set an alarm on your phone.
example.fact: In 1884, delegates at the International Meridian Conference set up the system of 24 time zones anchored to the meridian running through Greenwich, England, standardizing clocks worldwide for the first time in history.

examples.hanzi: 我把闹钟设定在六点半。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ nàozhōng shèdìng zài liù diǎn bàn.
examples.english: I set the alarm for six thirty.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事的设定是在未来的火星上。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi de shèdìng shì zài wèilái de Huǒxīng shàng.
examples.english: This story is set on Mars in the future.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 挽 is to pull or draw back.
免 (miǎn) hints at the sound: 挽 wǎn is close to 晚 wǎn.
回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.

example.hanzi: 他努力挽回失去的信任。
example.pinyin: Tā nǔlì wǎnhuí shīqù de xìnrèn.
example.english: He worked hard to win back the trust he had lost.
example.fact: NASA's Apollo 13 mission suffered an oxygen tank explosion in April 1970, roughly 200,000 miles from Earth, but flight controllers and the crew improvised fixes using onboard materials to bring all three astronauts home safely.

examples.hanzi: 他想挽回这段感情，可是已经太晚了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng wǎnhuí zhè duàn gǎnqíng, kěshì yǐjīng tài wǎn le.
examples.english: He wanted to save the relationship, but it was already too late.

examples.hanzi: 道歉也无法挽回造成的损失。
examples.pinyin: Dàoqiàn yě wúfǎ wǎnhuí zàochéng de sǔnshī.
examples.english: An apology can't make up for the loss that was caused.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — a long journey; also in 远 far, 道 road.
䍃 (yáo) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 摇 yáo and 谣 yáo.
辶 (walk) — movement and distance, as in 过, 近, 进: 远 is a road that goes far.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuǎn; 元 also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 那颗星星距离我们非常遥远。
example.pinyin: Nà kē xīngxīng jùlí wǒmen fēicháng yáoyuǎn.
example.english: That star is extremely far from us.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is now more than 24 billion kilometers from Earth, making it the most distant human-made object in existence; its radio signals still take over 22 hours to reach us.

examples.hanzi: 他梦想着去遥远的国家旅行。
examples.pinyin: Tā mèngxiǎng zhe qù yáoyuǎn de guójiā lǚxíng.
examples.english: He dreams of traveling to a distant country.

examples.hanzi: 那些快乐的日子已经很遥远了。
examples.pinyin: Nàxiē kuàilè de rìzi yǐjīng hěn yáoyuǎn le.
examples.english: Those happy days are already far away.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 许多游客前来参观故宫。
example.pinyin: Xǔduō yóukè qiánlái cānguān Gùgōng.
example.english: Many tourists come to visit the Forbidden City.
example.fact: Beijing's Forbidden City, completed in 1420, contains 980 surviving buildings and nearly 9,000 rooms, and served as the imperial palace for 24 emperors across the Ming and Qing dynasties.

examples.hanzi: 欢迎各位前来参加我们的开业典礼。
examples.pinyin: Huānyíng gèwèi qiánlái cānjiā wǒmen de kāiyè diǎnlǐ.
examples.english: Welcome, everyone, to our grand opening.

examples.hanzi: 很多家长前来接孩子放学。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō jiāzhǎng qiánlái jiē háizi fàngxué.
examples.english: Many parents came to pick up their children from school.

components.note: 单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and language, as in 说 say, 语 language, 话 speech; 词 is a word or phrase.
司 (sī) hints at the sound: 词 cí is close, and 司 also gives 饲 sì and 祠 cí.

example.hanzi: 这本词典收录了十万个单词。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn cídiǎn shōulù le shí wàn gè dāncí.
example.english: This dictionary contains 100,000 words.
example.fact: The Oxford English Dictionary contains entries for over 600,000 words, and compiling its first edition, published in 1928, took editors more than 70 years from the project's original start.

examples.hanzi: 我每天背二十个英语单词。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān bèi èrshí gè Yīngyǔ dāncí.
examples.english: I memorize twenty English words every day.

examples.hanzi: 这个单词的意思我不太清楚，请查一下词典。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dāncí de yìsi wǒ bù tài qīngchu, qǐng chá yīxià cídiǎn.
examples.english: I'm not sure what this word means, so please look it up in the dictionary.

components.note: 王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迷 is losing one's way.
米 (mǐ) — near sound — 迷 is mí, the same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 世界杯期间,球迷们彻夜狂欢。
example.pinyin: Shìjièbēi qījiān, qiúmímen chèyè kuánghuān.
example.english: During the World Cup, fans celebrate all night.
example.fact: The 2014 FIFA World Cup final in Brazil drew a global television audience estimated at over one billion viewers, making it one of the most-watched sporting events in human history.

examples.hanzi: 这位球星有很多忠实的球迷。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi qiúxīng yǒu hěn duō zhōngshí de qiúmí.
examples.english: This star player has many loyal fans.

examples.hanzi: 球迷们在体育场外等着球员出来。
examples.pinyin: Qiúmímen zài tǐyùchǎng wài děng zhe qiúyuán chūlái.
examples.english: The fans waited outside the stadium for the players to come out.

components.note: 彡 (hair strokes, decoration) — patterns and appearance: 形 shape, 影 shadow, 须 beard; 彩 is colorful decoration.
采 (cǎi) sounds exactly like 彩; also in 菜 cài and 踩 cǎi.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — arranging and moving by hand: 打, 推, 拉; 排 is to line things up.
非 (fēi) is a loose sound hint; its series includes 悲 bēi and 菲 fēi.

example.hanzi: 演员们正在为首演彩排。
example.pinyin: Yǎnyuánmen zhèngzài wèi shǒuyǎn cǎipái.
example.english: The actors are rehearsing for opening night.
example.fact: In January 1967, a flash fire broke out aboard Apollo 1 during a launch-pad rehearsal, killing all three astronauts and prompting NASA to redesign the capsule's hatch, materials, and safety procedures before any further crewed flights.

examples.hanzi: 明天晚上要进行最后一次彩排。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǎnshang yào jìnxíng zuìhòu yī cì cǎipái.
examples.english: The final rehearsal will be tomorrow night.

examples.hanzi: 婚礼前，他们先在教堂彩排了一遍。
examples.pinyin: Hūnlǐ qián, tāmen xiān zài jiàotáng cǎipái le yī biàn.
examples.english: Before the wedding, they ran through a rehearsal at the church.

components.note: 氏 is a plain unit; the dictionary reads it as a person bowing down, but its origin is debated. Meaning: clan or family name, as in 姓氏, 氏族, 摄氏 Celsius.

example.hanzi: 这个姓氏很少见。
example.pinyin: Zhège xìngshì hěn shǎojiàn.
example.english: This surname is quite rare.
example.fact: 氏 is a bound form. 姓氏 is 'surname', and 摄氏度 (Celsius) and 华氏度 (Fahrenheit) use 氏 after the scientist's surname. Anciently 氏 marked a clan branch while 姓 marked the lineage.

examples.hanzi: 美国常用华氏温度。
examples.pinyin: Měiguó chángyòng huáshì wēndù.
examples.english: The US commonly uses Fahrenheit.

examples.hanzi: 今天的气温是摄氏二十度。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de qìwēn shì shèshì èrshí dù.
examples.english: Today's temperature is twenty degrees Celsius.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds: 难, 雀, 雄; 集 is birds 隹 gathered on a tree 木: to gather.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).

example.hanzi: 学校组织了一次集体旅行。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào zǔzhī le yī cì jítǐ lǚxíng.
example.english: The school organized a group trip.
example.fact: Flocks of starlings can form massive, shifting shapes called murmurations, sometimes involving hundreds of thousands of birds that coordinate their movements within a fraction of a second of each other, with no leader directing the group.

examples.hanzi: 这是我们全班的集体照。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen quán bān de jítǐ zhào.
examples.english: This is our whole class's group photo.

examples.hanzi: 他把个人利益放在集体利益之后。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ gèrén lìyì fàng zài jítǐ lìyì zhīhòu.
examples.english: He puts personal interests behind the collective interest.

meanings: to put one's hand to it
to start out on a task

components.note: 著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 政府已经着手解决交通问题。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ yǐjīng zhuóshǒu jiějué jiāotōng wèntí.
example.english: The government has begun to address the traffic problem.
example.fact: In 1956, the United States began construction of its Interstate Highway System under President Eisenhower, eventually building over 77,000 kilometers of roadway in what was then the largest public works project in the country's history.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该马上着手准备明天的会议。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi mǎshàng zhuóshǒu zhǔnbèi míngtiān de huìyì.
examples.english: We should start preparing for tomorrow's meeting right away.

examples.hanzi: 不知道从哪里着手，他很发愁。
examples.pinyin: Bù zhīdào cóng nǎlǐ zhuóshǒu, tā hěn fāchóu.
examples.english: He didn't know where to begin and felt worried.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.
三 — three strokes, one more than 二. The numbers 一 二 三 are the only ones counted by drawing lines.

example.hanzi: 我们星期三有一场考试。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xīngqīsān yǒu yī chǎng kǎoshì.
example.english: We have an exam on Wednesday.
example.fact: The English name 'Wednesday' comes from 'Woden's day,' honoring the Germanic god Woden (Odin), while several Romance languages, such as Spanish 'miércoles,' instead preserve the older Roman name for Mercury's day.

examples.hanzi: 星期三是我最忙的一天。
examples.pinyin: Xīngqīsān shì wǒ zuì máng de yī tiān.
examples.english: Wednesday is my busiest day.

examples.hanzi: 我们约在星期三晚上七点见面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yuē zài xīngqīsān wǎnshang qī diǎn jiànmiàn.
examples.english: We agreed to meet at seven on Wednesday evening.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand holding a stick, as in 教 teach, 收 collect, 放 release: correcting by hand.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for gǎi.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.

example.hanzi: 工程师不断改进产品的设计。
example.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī bùduàn gǎijìn chǎnpǐn de shèjì.
example.english: Engineers keep improving the product's design.
example.fact: Toyota's production system popularized 'kaizen,' a philosophy of continuous incremental improvement that empowers factory workers to halt the assembly line themselves the moment they spot a defect, rather than letting problems pile up downstream.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章还有很多需要改进的地方。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng hái yǒu hěn duō xūyào gǎijìn de dìfang.
examples.english: This article still has many places that need improvement.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你的建议，我们会继续改进服务。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de jiànyì, wǒmen huì jìxù gǎijìn fúwù.
examples.english: Thank you for your suggestion, we will keep improving our service.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 洋 is the ocean, as in 海 sea, 河 river.
羊 (yáng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 样 yàng, 养 yǎng and 详 xiáng.
艹 (grass) — plants; 葱 is the onion, as in 草 grass, 菜 vegetable.
怱 (cōng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 聪 cōng and 匆 cōng.

example.hanzi: 妈妈在切洋葱的时候流眼泪了。
example.pinyin: Māma zài qiē yángcōng de shíhòu liú yǎnlèi le.
example.english: Mom cried while cutting onions.
example.fact: Cutting an onion ruptures its cells and triggers a chemical reaction that produces syn-propanethial-S-oxide, a volatile gas that drifts up and irritates the eyes, causing the classic reflexive tears.

examples.hanzi: 洋葱炒鸡蛋是我最爱吃的一道家常菜。
examples.pinyin: Yángcōng chǎo jīdàn shì wǒ zuì ài chī de yī dào jiācháng cài.
examples.english: Stir-fried onion with eggs is my favorite home dish.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我买两个洋葱和一斤土豆。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ mǎi liǎng gè yángcōng hé yī jīn tǔdòu.
examples.english: Please buy me two onions and a pound of potatoes.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
钅 (metal, simplified 金) — the metal bit held in a horse's mouth, hence to hold in the mouth; 衔 is also a rank or title.
行 (xíng) gives a close sound for xián.

example.hanzi: 他获得了博士头衔。
example.pinyin: Tā huòdé le bóshì tóuxián.
example.english: He earned the title of doctor.
example.fact: Guinness World Records lists the full ceremonial name of Bangkok as one of the longest place names in the world, running 169 letters, even though residents and official maps simply shorten it to Krung Thep.

examples.hanzi: 他的头衔是公司的副总经理。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tóuxián shì gōngsī de fù zǒngjīnglǐ.
examples.english: His title is deputy general manager of the company.

examples.hanzi: 她不在乎头衔，只想做好自己的工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù zàihu tóuxián, zhǐ xiǎng zuò hǎo zìjǐ de gōngzuò.
examples.english: She doesn't care about titles and just wants to do her job well.
